object_types.name: Person
object_types.definition: An individual tracked in the system, identified by a unique person ID. All persons in the system, including employees and managers, are instances of Person.

source_references.excerpt: We track persons generally -- anyone in the system is a person with a person ID.

object_types.name: PersonId
object_types.definition: The unique identifier assigned to each Person.

source_references.excerpt: a person with a person ID

object_types.name: Employee
object_types.definition: A person employed by the organization. Every employee is also a person, identified through their person ID.

source_references.excerpt: Employees are persons; every employee is also a person, identified the same way.

object_types.name: Manager
object_types.definition: An employee with extra responsibilities. Every manager is an employee, and through that, a person.

source_references.excerpt: A manager is an employee with extra responsibilities. Every manager is an employee, and through that, a person.

object_types.name: Department
object_types.definition: An organizational unit with employees. Each department has a unique department code and a unique department name.

source_references.excerpt: Every employee works in exactly one department.

object_types.name: DepartmentCode
object_types.definition: The unique identifier assigned to each Department.

source_references.excerpt: Each department has a department code.

object_types.name: DepartmentName
object_types.definition: The name of a department, such as 'Payroll' or 'Field Operations'. Department names are unique.

source_references.excerpt: Departments also each have a department name, like "Payroll" or "Field Operations", and no two share a name.

ambiguities.description: Department management direction and mandatory participation unclear. The transcript states 'A manager manages at most one department' and 'Some managers are between assignments and manage none.' This leaves ambiguous whether every department must have a manager. Is the 'is managed by' role on Department mandatory (every department must have a manager), or optional (a department can exist without a manager)? The forward direction states managers can manage zero or one department, but the reverse direction is not explicitly addressed.

source_references.excerpt: A manager manages at most one department. Some managers are between assignments and manage none.

ambiguities.description: Many-to-many possibility for 'Employee works in Department'. While the transcript states 'Every employee works in exactly one department' and 'nobody is in two departments at once', it is not explicitly clear whether a department can have only one employee, or whether departments employ many. The wording implies departments have many employees, but this should be confirmed. Is 'employs' on Department optional or mandatory? Can a department have zero employees?

source_references.excerpt: Every employee works in exactly one department. Departments have many employees, but nobody is in two departments at once, and nobody is unassigned.
